policies.text:
# Metropolis Hackathon Rules & Guidelines

**Terms & Conditions**

**Last Updated:** 3 September 2026 **Hackathon Period:** September 1, 2026 to November 3, 2026

## 1. ACCEPTANCE OF TERMS

By registering for, participating in, or submitting a project to the Metropolis Hackathon (the
"Hackathon"), you ("Participant," "you," or "your") agree to be bound by these Terms & Conditions
(the "Terms"). If you do not agree to these Terms, you may not participate in the Hackathon.

These Terms constitute a legally binding agreement between you and the Monad Foundation (the
"Organizer," "we," "us," or "our").

Third parties that fund prizes or bounties, provide credits or infrastructure, or otherwise support
the Hackathon (each, a "Sponsor") are not parties to these Terms. A Sponsor has no obligation to you
except as expressly set out in terms published by that Sponsor.

We may amend these Terms at any time by posting an updated version to the Hackathon website, and the
amended version applies from the date it is posted. We may also modify, suspend, postpone, or cancel
the Hackathon or any part of it, including tracks, dates, judging criteria, judges, prize amounts,
and in-person activations, where we consider it necessary or appropriate. If you do not accept an
amendment, your remedy is to stop participating.

These terms supplement, and do not replace, the Monad Foundation Terms of Service available at
www.monad.xyz/terms-of-service (the "Website Terms"), which are incorporated into these Terms by
reference and which you accept by registering for the Hackathon.

## 2. ELIGIBILITY

### 2.1 Age Requirements

Participants must be at least 18 years of age as of September 1, 2026. Participants under 18 may
participate only with verifiable parental or legal guardian consent.

### 2.2 Geographic Restrictions

The Hackathon is open to participants worldwide, except where prohibited by law. Participants must
not be, and must not be owned or controlled by or acting on behalf of, a person that is (a) resident
in, located in, or organized under the laws of a jurisdiction subject to comprehensive sanctions by
the United States, European Union, or United Nations or named on any sanctions or restricted party
list maintained by those authorities. We may screen registration details and wallet addresses against
those lists, and may refuse a registration, disqualify a submission, or withhold a prize on that
basis.

**Restricted Jurisdictions include but are not limited to:**

- Countries under U.S. OFAC sanctions
- Countries under EU sanctions
- Any jurisdiction where participation would violate local law
- Any jurisdiction added to this list by the Organizer during the Hackathon period, on notice posted
  to the Hackathon website

### 2.3 Employment Restrictions

Employees, contractors, and immediate family members, Organizer, any Sponsor, and any member of the
judging panel are not eligible to win prizes but may participate for educational purposes.

### 2.4 Team Participation

- Teams may consist of 1-5 members
- Each team must register for the Hackathon through the Hackathon website
- All team members must meet eligibility requirements
- One team member must be designated as the primary contact
- Prize money will be paid to the designated contact, who is responsible for distribution

### 2.5 Multiple Submissions

- Participants are only allowed to submit one project. Multiple submissions are not allowed.
- Each submission must compete in only one track
- Participants cannot win multiple main track prizes for the same project

## 3. HACKATHON OVERVIEW

### 3.1 Objective

Build and ship new products on the Monad blockchain across the four tracks described in Section 3.3,
each supported by a working prototype, public source code, a demo video, and documentation.

### 3.2 Prize Structure

**Total Prize Pool: $145,000 USD**

**Overall Winner ($25,000 total):**

- 1 Overall Winner: $25,000 USD, awarded to the most standout project across all tracks

**Track Prizes ($120,000 total):**

- $30,000 USD per track, across the four tracks described in Section 3.3
- Within each track, $10,000 USD awarded to each of the top three projects

**Additional Bounties:** Sponsor-funded bounties may be added and announced during the Hackathon
period, each with their own terms and requirements.

### 3.3 Tracks

The Hackathon is organized into four tracks. A submission may be entered in one track only.

- **Track 01 - Onchain Finance & Trading:** financial instruments, markets, and asset primitives,
  where the primary user is a trader, protocol, or financial product builder
- **Track 02 - Consumer Products & Payments:** products whose primary user is a consumer who may not
  identify as a crypto user, and whose core value is a financial experience rather than a trading or
  market making product
- **Track 03 - Social, Attention & Culture:** products whose core user value is social connection,
  cultural participation, or community, even where financial mechanics are involved
- **Track 04 - Trust, Identity & AI Infrastructure:** protocols, primitives, or infrastructure layers
  that other applications build on, rather than standalone consumer products

Every track requires a working product deployed on Monad, public source code on GitHub, a demo video,
and documentation, in each case as described in Section 4.

For Sponsor bounties: the submission must meet the requirements published by the relevant Sponsor for
that bounty

### 3.4 No Offer of Investment or Further Funding

Participation in the Hackathon does not entitle any Participant to an investment, grant, token
allocation, accelerator place, or any other funding from the Organizer or any Sponsor. Any reference
to venture support, mentorship, or downstream programmes describes opportunities that may become
available and is not an offer, a commitment, or a solicitation. Any funding, if it occurs, would be
made only under a separate written agreement and subject to the Organizer's own diligence and
approval.

## 4. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

### 4.1 Mandatory Requirements

All submissions must include:

**1. Public GitHub Repository** containing:

- Complete source code;
- README with setup instructions;
- Open source license (MIT, Apache 2.0, GPL, or similar);
- Clear attribution of external code/libraries used; and
- A commit history covering the build window.

**2. Demo Video (3 minutes):**

- Publicly accessible (YouTube, Loom, Vimeo, etc.);
- Clearly demonstrates the product in actual operation; and
- Shows Monad blockchain integration.

**3. Monad Integration:**

- Clear explanation of how the project leverages Monad;
- Contract addresses (if applicable); and
- Deployment to Monad mainnet or testnet.

**4. Originality and Build Window:**

- The substantial majority of the work submitted must be created during the Hackathon period;
- Pre-existing code or products may be used as a foundation only if the pre-existing components are
  identified in the README and the submission adds substantial new functionality built during the
  Hackathon period; and
- Use of AI coding tools is permitted and must be disclosed in the README.

**5. Documentation:**

- Project description
- Architecture overview
- Technology stack
- Setup/deployment instructions

**6. Submission Platform:** all submissions must be made through the Hackathon website. Use of the
Hackathon website is subject to its own terms of use and privacy policy, which apply in addition to
these Terms.

### 4.2 Submission Deadline

**Final Deadline: October 13, 2026, 11:59 PM ET**

- Submissions accepted on rolling basis starting September 1, 2026
- Late submissions will not be accepted
- Submission timestamp determined by the time recorded by the Hackathon website
- A submission may be edited until the deadline. The version recorded at the deadline is the version
  judged.

### 4.3 Submission Ownership

By submitting a project, you confirm that:

- You own all rights to the submission or have proper authorization
- The submission is your original work
- The submission does not infringe on any third-party rights
- You have properly attributed all external code and resources
- The submission contains no confidential information belonging to you or to a third party, including
  any current or former employer
- Your participation and your submission do not breach any agreement you have with an employer or
  client, including any assignment of inventions provision

## 5. JUDGING & WINNER SELECTION

### 5.1 Judging Process

- **Judging Period:** submissions are reviewed between October 14 and October 27, 2026
- **Judging Panel:** submissions are scored by judges selected by the Organizer. The Organizer may
  add, remove, or replace a judge at any time
- **Winner Announcement:** Winners announced on November 3, 2026

### 5.2 Judging Criteria

**All Tracks:**

- Product Quality & Completeness (20%)
- Technical Excellence (20%)
- Monad Integration (20%)
- Track Fit & Problem Relevance (20%)
- Innovation & Impact (20%)

**Sponsor Bounties:**

- Adherence to the published bounty requirements (40%)
- Technical Implementation (30%)
- Monad Integration (20%)
- Innovation (10%)

### 5.3 Conflicts of Interest and Non-Confidentiality of Submissions

- Judges and mentors include investors and operators who evaluate, fund, and build products in the
  same categories as the tracks. Submissions are reviewed on a non-confidential basis
- Nothing in these Terms creates a confidential relationship, a fiduciary duty, or any exclusivity
  between a Participant and the Organizer, a Sponsor, a judge, or a mentor
- The Organizer, Sponsors, judges, and mentors may independently develop, fund, or acquire products
  similar to a submission, and owe no obligation to a Participant in doing so
- Do not submit anything you are unwilling to disclose publicly, and do not include trade secrets,
  private keys, credentials, or third-party personal data in a submission

### 5.4 Judge Decisions

- All judging decisions are final and binding
- Judges may disqualify submissions that violate Terms
- Organizer reserves right to not award prizes if quality threshold is not met
- No appeals process; decisions are at sole discretion of judges

## 6. PRIZES

### 6.1 Prize Payment

- Prizes paid in USDC or equivalent stablecoin
- Payment within 30 days of the later of the winner announcement or completes the verification steps
  described below
- Payment to designated contact's provided wallet address
- Recipients may be required to undergo a KYC verification process

### 6.2 Taxes

- Winners are solely responsible for all taxes on prizes
- Winners responsible for compliance with local tax laws

### 6.3 Prize Forfeiture

Prizes may be forfeited if:

- Winner fails to provide required information (wallet address, KYC, etc.)
- Winner is found ineligible or in violation of Terms
- Winner's project is found to have plagiarized or violated IP rights

### 6.4 No Prize Substitution

- Prizes cannot be transferred, assigned, or substituted
- Cash value cannot be exchanged for other prizes
- Organizer reserves right to substitute prizes of equal or greater value if necessary

## 7. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

### 7.1 Ownership

Participants retain full ownership of their submissions. By participating, you grant Organizer and
each Sponsor:

- Perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to:
- Reproduce, display, and distribute your submission
- Use your project name, description, and demo materials
- Feature your project in marketing and promotional materials
- Create derivative works for promotional purposes only

### 7.2 Open Source Requirement

All submissions must be open source under an OSI-approved license such as:

- MIT License
- Apache License 2.0
- GNU General Public License (GPL)
- BSD License

Code must be publicly accessible on GitHub throughout and after the Hackathon.

### 7.3 Third-Party Rights

Participants are solely responsible for:

- Obtaining necessary rights for third-party code/assets
- Proper attribution of external resources
- Compliance with third-party licenses
- Ensuring no infringement of patents, copyrights, or trademarks

### 7.4 Organizer IP

The Hackathon name, logo, branding, and materials, and the Monad and Metropolis names, logos, and
marks, remain property of Organizer and its licensors. Participants may not use Hackathon branding
beyond the scope of participation without written permission.

## 8. CODE OF CONDUCT

### 8.1 Expected Behavior

Participants must:

- Treat all participants, judges, and organizers with respect
- Engage in constructive communication
- Respect diverse perspectives and backgrounds
- Comply with all Discord and community guidelines
- Provide honest and accurate information

### 8.2 Prohibited Behavior

The following are strictly prohibited:

- Harassment, discrimination, or hate speech
- Cheating, plagiarism, or misrepresentation
- Submitting malicious code or security vulnerabilities
- Market manipulation or wash trading (for tokens)
- Spamming, brigading, or disruptive behavior
- Violations of applicable laws or regulations

### 8.3 Enforcement

Violations may result in:

- Warning from organizers
- Removal from Discord/community
- Disqualification from Hackathon
- Forfeiture of prizes
- Referral to appropriate authorities for illegal conduct

## 9. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

### 9.1 Product Requirements

Projects must demonstrate a working implementation:

- A functioning prototype, not a mockup, design file, or concept deck
- Code a third party can run by following the README
- A clear statement of the problem the product solves and the intended user
- Evidence of the product operating in the demo video

### 9.2 Monad Integration Requirements

All projects must:

- Provide contract addresses or transaction hashes
- Use Monad mainnet or testnet
- Clearly document blockchain integration purpose
- Demonstrate why Monad's capabilities are utilized

### 9.3 Token Requirements (Optional)

Tokens are not required in any track. Where a submission includes a token:

- The Participant is solely responsible for the legal treatment of that token, including any
  securities, financial promotion, and consumer protection requirements in each jurisdiction where it
  is offered
- The token must not be described as issued, endorsed, or approved by the Organizer or any Sponsor

### 9.4 Demo Video Requirements

Demo videos must:

- Be no more than 3 minutes in length
- Be publicly accessible via YouTube, Loom, Vimeo, or similar
- Show the product in actual operation (not mockups or slides)
- Show Monad blockchain interactions

## 10. DISQUALIFICATION

### 10.1 Grounds for Disqualification

Submissions may be disqualified for:

- Violating any of these Terms
- Submitting after deadline
- Missing required components
- Plagiarism or copyright infringement
- Submitting malicious or harmful code
- Market manipulation of tokens
- Providing false or misleading information
- Violating Code of Conduct
- Failing to meet eligibility requirements

### 10.2 Security & Malicious Code

Projects containing malicious code will be immediately disqualified:

- Malware, viruses, or trojans
- Exploits targeting users or infrastructure
- Backdoors or unauthorized access mechanisms
- Code designed to harm or deceive users

Participants responsible for malicious submissions may be banned from future events and reported to
authorities.

### 10.3 Plagiarism

- Copying substantial portions of code without attribution
- Submitting another person's work as your own
- Forking projects without significant original contributions
- Failure to properly credit external libraries/resources

### 10.4 Token Market Manipulation (Where a Submission Includes a Token)

The following are prohibited and grounds for disqualification:

- Wash trading or fake volume
- Coordinated pump and dump schemes
- Bot manipulation of token price
- Misrepresenting token supply or liquidity
- False claims about token utility or partnerships

## 11. LIABILITY & DISCLAIMERS

### 11.1 Organizer Liability

TO THE MAXIMUM EXTENT PERMITTED BY LAW:

The Hackathon, and all related materials are provided on an "as is" and "as available" basis, without
warranty of any kind, whether express or implied.

Organizer and Sponsor are not liable for:

- Technical difficulties, server outages, or network issues
- Lost, late, incomplete, or corrupted submissions
- Unauthorized access to submissions
- Errors in prize distribution or judging
- Token value fluctuations or losses
- Smart contract bugs or exploits
- Participant disputes or conflicts
- Any indirect, incidental, or consequential damages

### 11.2 Participant Representations

By participating, you represent and warrant that:

- All information provided is accurate and complete
- Your submission complies with all applicable laws
- You have all necessary rights and permissions
- Your project does not infringe third-party rights
- You accept all risks associated with blockchain/crypto

### 11.3 Indemnification

The indemnity in Section 6.4 of the Website Terms applies to your participation in the Hackathon. In
addition, and without limiting it:

You agree to indemnify and hold harmless Organizer, Sponsor, judges, and affiliates from:

- Any claims arising from your participation
- Any claims arising from your submission
- Violations of these Terms
- Infringement of third-party rights
- Any harm caused by your project or token

## 12. PRIVACY & DATA

### 12.1 Information Collection

We collect:

- Registration information (name, email, country)
- Submission materials (code, videos, documentation)
- Contact information (Discord, Twitter, GitHub, LinkedIn)
- Communication history
- Wallet addresses for prize distribution

### 12.2 Use of Information

Information is used to:

- Administer the Hackathon
- Communicate with participants
- Evaluate submissions
- Distribute prizes
- Promote winners and projects
- Improve future events

### 12.3 Public Information

The following may be made public:

- Project names and descriptions
- Demo videos and documentation
- Winner announcements

### 12.4 Third-Party Sharing

Information may be shared with:

- Sponsor, in relation to their bounties and prizes
- Judging panel
- DeltaV and other platforms used to run the Hackathon
- Service providers (payment processors, KYC providers)
- As required by law

## 13. MISCELLANEOUS

### 13.1 Entire Agreement

These Terms constitute the entire agreement between participants and Organizer regarding the
Hackathon and supersede all prior agreements or understandings, other than the terms of use of the
Hackathon website and any Sponsor's separate bounty terms, which apply in addition to these Terms.

### 13.2 Severability

If any provision is found unenforceable, remaining provisions remain in full force and effect.

### 13.3 Waiver

Failure to enforce any provision does not constitute a waiver of that provision or any other
provision.

### 13.4 Assignment

Participants may not assign or transfer their rights or obligations under these Terms. Organizer may
assign these Terms without restriction.

### 13.5 Publicity

Winners agree to participate in reasonable publicity efforts including:

- Winner announcements and press releases
- Social media features and blog posts
- Case studies and project showcases
- Event recaps and promotional materials

Winners may decline excessive or unreasonable publicity requests.

### 13.6 No Partnership

Nothing in these Terms creates a partnership, joint venture, employment, or agency relationship
between participants and Organizer.

### 13.7 Headings

Section headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation.

### 13.8 Language

These Terms are provided in English. Any translations are for convenience only; the English version
controls.

## 14. ACKNOWLEDGMENT & ACCEPTANCE

By registering for the Hackathon, you acknowledge that:

- You have read and understood these Terms in full
- You agree to be bound by these Terms
- You meet all eligibility requirements
- You will comply with all rules and requirements
- You accept all risks associated with participation
- You understand judging decisions are final
- You understand prizes are subject to tax obligations
- You grant licenses as described in Section 7
